lines.trans: Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Salma, he did not make the brass-polish face!
Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?

words.gram: def f sg noun with ha- (this)

lines.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.

words.gloss: for; because of; in order to

lines.trans: Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mr Tough Judge!
Eat all you want, Mazen, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!

words.gloss: as much as; the size of

Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.
Wait... let a man chew properly before you two start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Salma, he did not make the brass-polish face!
Well, Mazen? Tell us honestly—is that worthy of our Saturday anniversary table?

He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.

Eat all you want, Mazen, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!

Here goes Judge Mazen with forkful number one—nobody say a word!
Notice how the fork glides straight through without a hammer or safety goggles.

words.gram: def f sg noun with ha- (this)

lines.trans: Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Nour.
He is writing in capital letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! Ten out of ten in Mazen pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for structural safety, however, I should test one more small corner slice.

words.gloss: for; because of; in order to

lines.trans: Aha! Caught you asking for seconds, Mr Tough Judge!
Eat all you want, Mazen, and write down four full cakes for Saturday!

words.gloss: as much as; the size of

lines.trans: Keep baking like this, Salma, and half of Amman will line up outside our gate.
Goodbye!

meanings.note: Exclamation when a puzzle clicks into place ('aha!').

examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand the whole story!
Aha, that is why you took the bus!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: I bought four books.
The guests arrived at four in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باكل, بياكل).

examples.trans: The brothers are eating lemon cake in the courtyard.
We ate a hot breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أباريق.

examples.trans: The teapot is hot on the table.
Pour the hot water into the teapot.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking بـ for what is celebrated.

examples.text: رح نحتفل بافتتاح الكافيه مع كل الجيران.
examples.trans: We're going to celebrate the café opening with all the neighbours.

examples.text: احتفلنا لما خلص دهان الشيش قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We celebrated when the shutter painting finished before dusk.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking a direct object.

examples.text: لازم نختبر حرارة الفرن قبل ما ندخل الصينية.
examples.trans: We need to test the oven temperature before putting the tin in.

examples.text: مازن بختبر كل وصفة بدقة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Mazen tests every recipe with great precision.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian Form X verb (بيستاهل / بتستاهل) meaning 'to deserve, be worth it'.

examples.trans: The ovens deserve a break after baking!

examples.text: انتي بتستاهلي كل خير يا سلمى.
examples.trans: You deserve every good thing, Salma.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait just a minute.

examples.text: استنى شوي، أنا نازل معك هسه!
examples.trans: Wait a second—I'm coming down with you right now!

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.trans: Our weekend is on Saturday.

examples.text: يوم السبت الصبح دايماً بنروح نجيب خضرة من السوق.
examples.trans: On Saturday morning we always go buy vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: Levantine passive Form VII of حط ('to put/place').

examples.trans: The new tables were placed under the arch.
The green ledger was put away in the attic chest.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: The kids are playing outside.

examples.text: الأولاد بلعبوا برا بالساحة جنب الشجر.
examples.trans: The children are playing outside in the courtyard beside the trees.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلش, بيبلش).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started heating up right away!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Used to indicate first-person possession.

examples.trans: This book is mine, not yours.
My notebook is still open on the table.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: I only want two pieces, two are enough.

examples.text: جبنا كتابين تنين من رف الإعارة.
examples.trans: We brought two books from the lending shelf.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine colloquial word for 'someone' or 'anyone' (in negative sentences).

examples.trans: Is anyone here?

examples.text: في حدا بعرف وين نحفظت الخريطة؟
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the map was stored?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حروف.

examples.trans: Two small letters are written on the corner.
The letters of her name are clear on the zip.

meanings.note: Formal honorific title meaning 'Your/Esteemed Presence', used in official speeches.

examples.text: نرحب بحضرة المدير العام وبكل الضيوف الكرام.
examples.trans: We welcome the esteemed General Director and all our honored guests.
Have you (formal) been working in this building for a long time?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Essential Jordanian word used for giving directions ('go straight') or to mean doing something immediately.

examples.trans: Walk straight and then turn right.

examples.text: امشي دغري لعند القوس وبعدين لف يسار.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the arch and then turn left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ذهب (gold); also pronounced دهبي in everyday Jordanian.

examples.text: اخبزي الكيكة ليصير لونها ذهبي حلو.
examples.trans: Bake the cake until its colour turns a lovely golden.
She won a gold medal in the cooking competition.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: Write with a pencil so you can erase it.

examples.text: الرقم مكتوب بقلم رصاص خفيف جنب الزاوية.
examples.trans: The number is written in light pencil near the corner.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine/Jordanian word for 'man / guy' (plural: زلم). Warm and conversational.

examples.text: الزلمة اللي قص القماش جاهز من زمان!
examples.trans: The man who cut the cloth was ready long ago!
Tariq is a kind man with a big heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسجل, بيسجل).

examples.text: سجلنا بالغلط حجزين على غرفة سبعة!
examples.trans: By mistake we booked two reservations into room seven!
I wrote the name down in the big ledger.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Spoken defective verb meaning 'to be worth' (يسوى / بتسوى). Distinct from سوّى ('to do/make').

examples.text: الراحة بعد التعب بتسوى الدنيا كلها.
examples.trans: Rest after hard work is worth the whole world.
How much is this rug worth in the market?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian tool word used in carpentry and household repairs; plural شواكيش.

examples.text: جيب الشاكوش من صندوق العدة عشان نثبت اللوح.
examples.trans: Bring the hammer from the toolbox so we can fasten the board.

examples.text: سمعنا صوت شاكوش بطرق بالورشة تحت.
examples.trans: We heard the sound of a hammer knocking in the workshop below.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial Jordanian noun for a broken piece, slice, or scrap of paper, bread, or stone.

examples.text: لقينا شقفة ورق صغيرة تحت الباب.
examples.trans: We found a small scrap of paper under the door.

examples.text: اقسم الكيكة وعطي كل واحد شقفة متساوية.
examples.trans: Cut the cake and give everyone an equal piece.

meanings.note: Refers both to an eating fork at the table and a plant thorn; plural شوكات (or collective شوك for thorns).

examples.text: حطينا شوكة وسكينة جنب كل صحن.
examples.trans: We placed a fork and knife next to each plate.

examples.text: انتبهي من الشوكة على غصن الورد.
examples.trans: Watch out for the thorn on the rose branch.

meanings.note: Used constantly as بصراحة or bare صراحة ('honestly / to be frank').

examples.trans: Honestly, I loved the place very much.
Frankly, the coffee here is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صعبة, plural: صعبين).

examples.trans: Family disagreements are always hard.

examples.text: الزبدة المالحة صعبة مع المربى الحلو.
examples.trans: Salted butter is tricky with sweet jam.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: He stayed at home and didn't go out.

examples.text: ضل الدفتر مفتوح عالطاولة طول الليل.
examples.trans: The notebook remained open on the table all night.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a waiting line or queue at a shop or school; plural طوابير.

examples.text: في طابور طويل قدام المخبز الصبح.
examples.trans: There is a long queue in front of the bakery in the morning.

examples.text: وقفنا بالطابور بهدوء لحد ما وصل دورنا.
examples.trans: We stood quietly in line until our turn came.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: Put the things on the table.

examples.text: طاولة المطبخ مليانة علب بهارات ومرطبانات.
examples.trans: The kitchen table is full of spice tins and jars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: The time is ten o'clock right now.
The shop closes at ten o'clock at night.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغير, بيغير).

examples.trans: Rami changed his shirt three times!
We gave him a discount because we changed the room.

meanings.note: Defective noun on the faa'i pattern; drops final -y in indefinite nominative/genitive only in formal Arabic, kept as قاضي in Jordanian.

examples.trans: The judge asked to hear the two witnesses' statements.

examples.text: العم سالم معروف عند الجيران كأنه قاضي الحكيم.
examples.trans: Uncle Salem is known among the neighbours like a wise judge.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.trans: I have to arrive before five o'clock.

examples.text: غسلنا الفواكه منيح قبل ما نقطعها للتذوق.
examples.trans: We washed the fruit thoroughly before slicing it for the tasting.

قد.gloss: as much as; the size of

meanings.en: as much as; the size of
meanings.note: Expresses equal amount or degree: قدنا مرتين ('twice as much as us'), قد ما بقدر ('as much as I can').

examples.trans: Tariq is twice as curious as we are!
I tried to smile as much as I could!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; قلم رصاص means 'pencil'. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.trans: He wrote a long letter.

examples.text: الرسام كتب الملاحظات بالحبر الأسود عالهامش.
examples.trans: The illustrator wrote the notes in black ink in the margin.

meanings.note: Colloquial noun from كشّر (to frown/scowl); describes a sour or grumpy facial expression.

examples.text: تغيرت كشرة وجهه لضحكة أول ما ذاق العسل.
examples.trans: The frown on his face turned into a smile as soon as he tasted the honey.

examples.text: بلاش هالكشرة الصبح، اليوم رح يكون حلو.
examples.trans: Drop that morning frown; today is going to be good.

كشف.gloss: to uncover; to reveal; to inspect

meanings.en: to uncover; to reveal; to inspect
meanings.note: Form I verb taking direct objects or عن (about) when revealing a hidden clue or secret.

examples.text: الحرارة كشفت الحبر السري المكتوب عالورقة.
examples.trans: The heat revealed the secret ink written on the sheet.
The doctor examined the patient and reassured him.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.trans: I want tea, and also coffee.

examples.text: ذقنا التانية وكمان التالتة عشان نقارن القوام.
examples.trans: We tasted the second one and also the third to compare the texture.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How are you today?

examples.text: كيف قدرت تفتح القفل القديم بدون ما تكسره؟
examples.trans: How did you manage to open the old lock without breaking it?

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بلاحظ / لاحظت) from root ل-ح-ظ, common in both formal and everyday Jordanian speech.

examples.trans: Do you know what I noticed first?
I didn't notice that the window was open.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لقم.

examples.trans: Taste just one bite of the cake!
We had a quick bite before work.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Form I sound verb describing chewing food carefully, especially during tasting.

examples.text: مضغ اللقمة على مهله عشان يميز البهارات.
examples.trans: He chewed the bite slowly so he could tell the spices apart.

examples.text: امضغ الأكل منيح قبل ما تبلعه.
examples.trans: Chew the food well before swallowing it.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Loanword used both for competition medals and small keychains or pendant medallions.

examples.text: المفتاح مربوط بميدالية نحاس على شكل نجمة.
examples.trans: The key is attached to a star-shaped brass keychain.
He won a silver medal in the swimming competition.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بناول, بيناول).

examples.trans: Hand me the heavy iron wrench.
Pass me the teacup, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نجارين.

examples.text: النجار صنع الطاولة من خشب بلوط.
examples.trans: The carpenter built the table out of oak wood.
My grandfather was a master carpenter in the quarter.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: This jug is made of copper.

examples.text: الإبريق والمصفاية معمولين من نحاس مطروق قديم.
examples.trans: The teapot and strainer are made of old hammered copper.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: التقينا بالساحة الساعة تمانية ونص تماما.
examples.trans: We met in the courtyard at eight-thirty sharp.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Formal/educated yes-no question marker also heard in careful Jordanian speech; often omitted in casual speech.

examples.text: هل هادا هو الدفتر اللي كنت تدور عليه؟
examples.trans: Is this the notebook you were looking for?

examples.text: ما بعرف هل المكتبة فاتحة اليوم أو مسكرة.
examples.trans: I do not know whether the library is open today or closed.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.text: هيك الحياة، يوم الك ويوم عليك.
examples.trans: Such is life, one day for you and one day against you.

examples.text: ما تحكي معه هيك قدام الناس، احكي معه على جنب.
examples.trans: Don't talk to him like that in front of people; speak to him privately.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from هيكل (frame, structure, skeleton); feminine هيكلية.

examples.text: في رسم هيكلي للبيت جوا ملف المهندس.
examples.trans: There is a structural drawing of the house inside the architect's file.
We made a small structural adjustment to the plan.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian presentative word ('here is! / look!') pointing to someone or something right now; takes suffixes (هيهم hayy-hum 'here they are!').

examples.text: هي تاكسي وقف عند الباب هلا!
examples.trans: Look, a taxi just stopped at the door!
Here they come down the stairs!

meanings.note: Defective active participle of وقى (to protect); also used substantively in compounds like واقي شمس (sunscreen).

examples.text: حطينا غطا واقي فوق الخريطة عشان الرطوبة.
examples.trans: We put a protective cover over the map against humidity.

examples.text: لبس كفوف واقية قبل ما يمسك الصينية السخنة.
examples.trans: He put on protective gloves before holding the hot tin.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Casual loanword from English yes used playfully in celebratory speech when something succeeds.

examples.text: يس! الكيكة التانية طلعت مزبوطة مية بالمية!
examples.trans: Yes! The second cake turned out one hundred percent right!
Yes, the old lock finally opened!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
